steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

In a medium bowl, cream together the butter and brown sugar until smooth. Stir in the eggs, vanilla and honey. Sift together the flour, baking soda and cinnamon, gradually stir into the creamed mixture. Finally, stir in the rolled oats and raisins.
Drop dough by rounded teaspoonfuls onto unprepared cookie sheets. Bake for 10 to 15 minutes in the preheated oven, until cookies start to brown. Remove from baking sheets to cool on wire racks.

raw_recipe.headline: Oatmeal Raisin Cookies VI
raw_recipe.description: This is a really moist, delicious cookie that's also quite healthy.

review.reviewBody: In order to make these a bit "healthy" as the description says, I used olive oil in place of butter and wheat flour instead of white. Also used some nutmeg. Definitally good cookies, I managed to get my husband to clean the kitchen by promising to make them again. They're in the oven now. ^_-

This is a great base recipe using rolled oats (most oatmeal cookie recipes call for quick oats, but I prefer the texture with rolled oats). That said, this recipe definitely needs salt. I added a scant teaspoon.

I use this recipe as a foundation, and I often add quite a bit more sugar when I don't care about making them "healthy." Then, instead of the honey, I'll add 2/3 cup granulated sugar.

As a final note, since rolled oats are thicker than quick, I let the dough rest for a few hours at room temp (or up to 72 hours in the fridge) before cooking. The oats integrate really nicely then.

These are pretty good.

I couldn't find oatmeal around here (Asia) so I used barley meal instead. The malt made it way too sweet, so I'd suggest cutting the sugar by half.

Also, I was trying to do a Christmassy thing, so I used 40g molasses (instead of 20g honey) and added nutmeg and ginger.

If you're using rolled oats or barley; both of these are pretty dry and might upset your stomach; I suggest soaking the raisins and then taking water and all and mixing the raisins/water with your oats/barley. Let the barley/oats absorb all the water for a while, then use it as normal in the recipe.

Delicious! I too soaked the raisins. I ended up using 2 1/2 cups of oatmeal but I should have used all 3 cups, due to the soaked raisins the dough was quite wet. Added a little more flour to compensate but I think the oats would have been better. Also did 1/2 baking soda and 1 1/2 baking powder so they wouldn't be flat.
One last thing-due to some others saying how bland they were, I used APPLE PIE SPICE which gave it a great flavor! I used 2 tsps, I think a little more would have been even better. Otherwise, loved this cookie.

First time I followed the recipe ALMOST exact - my family doesn't care for raisins, so I always bake with craisins.
This second time I substituted 1/2c white flour with 1/2c whole wheat and added some nutmeg. 
First batch baked at 15 minutes - a little too long. Will do second batch at 12.
Perfect cookie. Everyone loves them. They are in demand.

I was married for ten years before I found out that Oatmeal Raisin Cookies were my husband's favorite. I made a half batch last week to test the recipe and a whole batch this morning, so we could share with the neighbors. I did add a teaspoon of salt to the sifted flour this time with a marked improvement in taste. I also flattened each cookie with a fork just a little bit before baking. This technique made for a more uniform shape. I used a cookie scoop and it made exactly four dozen cookies.

These are very good! Crispy around the edges, chewy in the middle. I used a bag of Trader Joe's Golden Berry Blend for variety (dried cranberries, blueberries, cherries and golden raisins. I confess to adding a bit of salt and a bit of ground nutmeg. Other than that, I left the recipe as is and they are delicious. I will make them again!
Added 1tsp. Salt and 1/4 tsp. Nutmeg, and didn’t add the honey, but otherwise followed the recipe exactly. Really good cookies,

Excellent cookie. Followed the recipe pretty much but added walnuts and white chocolate chips. Also salt. Also used half wheat flour. They are plenty sweet, probably because of the white chocolate, so next time I will reduce the sugar by half. These made a lot of cookies!

I had been looking for a recipe that I could sub some applesauce in for oil. This one worked well! I read a number of reviews and made some similar adjustments to other cooks. I used half margarine, half applesauce, and reduced the brown sugar. I substituted 1 c. whole wheat flour and a half cup ground flax for the all purpose. Just because I like spicy cookies, I added cloves, nutmeg, and ginger as well. I'm munching on them now as they cool down and they are delish...they aren't as moist with the modifications, but they are soft and not at all greasy.

I've made these a few times and they turn out so moist and chewy. I love a lot of raisins so I add another 1/2 cup and I used 1/2 cup of butter and 1/2 cup of unrefined coconut oil to cut down on the butter in this recipe!!
Quick and easy
My family and I love these cookies, they are delicious. I add more cinnamon (2tsp) & raisins (1.5 cups), I never over bake them, we like them a little soft and chewy.
I like this recipe. I made it as written except I added roasted pecans. They are sweet enough and the salted butter removes issue of blandness. Healthy and easy to make labels it a keeper in my book.
Great recipe! I used half the ingredients because I'm on a diet!! I also added nutmeg and they came out so delicious. I can't stop eating them!!!!
The BEST Oatmeal Cookies EVER!!
Very good, its my new recipe i will be using forever!!

The cookies were average. I made them as the recipe indicated but I think they came out a bit dry. I also took them out sooner as mentioned by other people. The taste was ok, but I've had better recipes. I do not think I will make them again. Also, I found it odd that they do not use salt and I am wondering if this is why the cookies did not taste as sweet as other recipes.
Delicious

Nice recipe. I make smaller cookies so this yields five dozen for me. I don't sift the flour etc - I just beat the butter, eggs, and vanilla (I omit the honey because I don't see the point) then dump in everything else and beat it for a minute. Quick and easy.
